# Figure provenance

**Every image in this repository was generated by our own code. None was
downloaded, none is stock art, and none was traced or copied from a paper.**

That is a checkable claim, not an assertion — run `python verify_figures.py`
from this folder.

---

## The evidence

A PNG file carries a `tEXt` metadata chunk. Matplotlib stamps its own name and
version into it on every save. All 22 PNGs in this repository carry:

```
Software: 'Matplotlib version3.10.9, https://matplotlib.org/'
```

An image downloaded from a paper, a website, or a stock library would carry
something else entirely — an EXIF block from a camera, an Adobe or GIMP
signature, or no `Software` chunk at all. None of ours does. `verify_figures.py`
reads the chunk out of every file and fails loudly on anything that is not
matplotlib-generated.

This is worth caring about because a figure lifted from a paper is a copyright
problem *and* an academic-integrity problem, and "we made it ourselves" is
hard to prove after the fact unless you can point at something concrete.

## What produced each figure, and from what data

| Figure | Type | Generated by | Input data |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fig01_mof_concept.png` | Schematic | `make_figures.py` | None — a drawn diagram explaining node + linker → framework |
| `fig02_pipeline.png` | Schematic | `make_figures.py` | None — the eight-stage pipeline, drawn |
| `fig03_periodic_vs_naive.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | `1_website/UiO-66.cif`, decomposed live |
| `fig04_degeneracy.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | `1_website/HKUST-1.cif`, centrality computed live |
| `fig05_defect.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | `1_website/HKUST-1.cif`, before/after linker removal |
| `fig06_boxgrowing.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | `1_website/HKUST-1.cif`, box-growing curves |
| `fig07_tau_fix.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | `3_notebooks/results.json` — the τ defect, before and after |
| `fig08_band77.png` | **Data** | `mof_band_analysis.ipynb`, Step 11 | `3_notebooks/results.json` — all 77 frameworks |
| `band77_figure.png` | **Data** | `mof_band_analysis.ipynb`, Step 11 | Same as fig08; this is the copy used in the deck |
| `band_analysis.png` | **Data** | `mof_band_analysis.ipynb`, Step 11 | `3_notebooks/results.json` |
| `network_analysis_figure.png` | **Data** | `make_figures.py` | The four demonstration CIFs, Laplacian spectra |

"Schematic" means the figure explains an idea rather than plotting a
measurement — the shapes and positions are chosen for clarity. Those two are
still drawn in matplotlib by our own script; they are not clip art. Everything
marked **Data** is a plot of numbers our pipeline computed, and the input file
is named so you can recompute it.

---

## The duplicates are deliberate

The same figure appears in more than one folder:

| File | Copies in | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `fig01`–`fig08` | `1_website/figures/`, `8_textbook/figures/` | The site must work from a `file://` clone with no build step, and the textbook must render on GitHub. Neither can reach across folders reliably, so each carries its own copy. |
| `band77_figure.png` | `4_reference/`, `7_presentation/`, `7_presentation/overleaf/` | LaTeX resolves `\includegraphics` relative to the `.tex` file, and the Overleaf zip has to be self-contained when uploaded. |

They are byte-identical copies of one generated file, not separately produced
images that could drift apart. `verify_figures.py` checks that by hashing them.

---

## Regenerating

```bash
cd 4_reference
pip install numpy matplotlib
python make_figures.py          # rewrites fig01–fig07 and network_analysis_figure
```

`fig08_band77.png` comes from the analysis notebook rather than this script,
because it plots all 77 spectra and needs the full `results.json`:

```bash
jupyter notebook ../3_notebooks/mof_band_analysis.ipynb   # Step 11
```

After regenerating, copy the outputs to the folders listed in the duplicates
table above, or run `python make_figures.py --sync` which does it for you.

---

## Verifying

```bash
cd 4_reference
python verify_figures.py
```

It checks three things and exits non-zero on any failure:

1. **Every PNG was produced by matplotlib** — reads the `Software` chunk.
2. **No PNG carries camera or image-editor metadata** — the signature of a
   downloaded or retouched image.
3. **Duplicated figures are byte-identical** — so a stale copy in one folder
   cannot silently disagree with the live one in another.
